{{Short description|Estonian chemist}}
{{More citations needed|date=December 2010}}

'''Hillar Muidar Rootare''' (26 April 1928 – 2 October 2008) was an Estonian-American physical chemist<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.wcacs.net/PN/WCLocalEvents.html|title=ACS Western Carolinas Section Local Events Page|year=2006|publisher=American Chemical Society|accessdate=13 December 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110724125109/http://www.wcacs.net/PN/WCLocalEvents.html|archive-date=24 July 2011|url-status=dead}}</ref> and materials scientist best known for his work in the development of [[mercury (element)|mercury]] [[porosimetry]], high pressure [[liquid chromatography]], and formulation of the [[Rootare-Prenzlow Equation]].

== Biography ==
Rootare was born and raised in [[Tallinn]], [[Estonia]], emigrated from [[Estonia]] to [[Helsinki]], [[Finland]], in 1944, and later to [[Visby]], on the [[Sweden|Swedish]] island of [[Gotland]], and immigrated to [[New York City]] in the United States from [[Sweden]] in 1946.<ref name="Obit">{{cite news |title=Hillar Rootare |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/121923361/hillar-rootare-1928-2008/ |work=The Atlanta Constitution |date=October 5, 2008 |location=Atlanta, GA |page=D17 |access-date=March 30, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> He attended Jersey City Junior College<ref>{{cite news |title=J. C. Students Get Princeton Degrees |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/121990477/hillar-rootare-1928-2008/ |work=The Jersey Journal |date=June 17, 1952 |location=Jersey City, NJ |page=7 |access-date=March 31, 2023 |via=[[Newspapers.com]]}} {{Open access}}</ref> and [[Wagner College]] on [[Staten Island]], [[New York (state)|New York]], and received his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Michigan]] in 1973. He was displaced several times during and after [[World War II]], and as a result he spoke several languages, including [[English language|English]], [[Estonian language|Estonian]], [[Finnish language|Finnish]], [[Swedish language|Swedish]], as well as, to a lesser degree, [[German language|German]] and [[Russian language|Russian]].<ref name="Obit"/> Hillar Rootare was the nephew of [[Estonia]]n [[Chess|chess player]] [[Vidrik Rootare]], several of whose games against the world-renowned International [[Grandmaster (chess)|Grand Master]] [[Paul Keres]] are published among Keres's most interesting games, and of [[Salme Rootare]], a Women's [[International Master]] in chess, and 15-time Estonian women's chess champion, who once finished third in the world chess championship competition (1959). Hillar's middle name, Muidar, is [[radium]] spelled backwards—he was given the name because his father, Karl Johannes Rootare, also a chemist,<ref name="Obit"/> was conducting some early experiments with radium and other radioactive materials around the time Hillar was born in 1928. Hillar's mother, Karin (Kangas) Rootare, was born in [[Narva]], [[Estonia]], and is of [[Ingrian Finns|Ingrian]]-[[Finns|Finnish]] as well as Estonian descent. Rootare and Carl Prenzlow came up with the [[Rootare-Prenzlow Equation]] while in graduate school at the [[University of Michigan]], in typical Estonian fashion over a late-night beer after working in the laboratory, working it out on cocktail napkins at Metzger's bar in [[Ann Arbor]]. Hillar, a former faculty member of the [[University of Michigan]] as well as a former student, was also a former president of the American Fine Particle Society (physics). He was an officer in the [[United States Air Force]], and served in the [[Korean War]] as a [[navigator]] aboard a [[B-17]] converted for reconnaissance. He married Norene (Kindstrand) Rootare since 1959.<ref name="Obit"/> They live in Atlanta, Georgia, in the United States, and have six children, Laura, Paul, Niel, Eva Marie, Lennart, and Margrethe. They also have relatives in Sweden and Estonia.<ref name="Obit"/>

==Publications==

Rootare is highly regarded in several areas, having published more than 100 papers and cited in hundreds more, but particularly so in the field of [[porosimetry]], where he considered one of the foremost experts, and is one of the most widely published chemists in the United States.{{Citation needed|date=June 2008}} <!-- over a hundred papers does make you one of the most published - several people have more than 1000 --> Examples of his published papers include:

* Solubility-Product Phenomena in Hydroxyapatite-Water Systems, H.M. Rootare, V.R. Deitz, & F.G. Carpenter, 17 Journal of Colloid Science p.&nbsp;179 (1962).
*Surface Areas from Mercury Porosimetry Measurements, Rootare, H.M., and Prenzlow, C.F., 71 Journal of Physical Chemistry p.&nbsp;2733 (1967).<ref>{{cite journal|title=Surface areas from mercury porosimeter measurements|date=July 1967|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry|volume=71|issue=8|pages=2733–2736|doi=10.1021/j100867a057|last1 = Rootare|first1 = Hillar M.|last2=Prenzlow|first2=Carl F.}}</ref>
* A Review of Mercury Porosimetry, H.M. Rootare, 5 Perspectives in Powder Metallurgy 225, Advanced Experimental Techniques in Powder Metallurgy, Plenum Press (New York, London 1970).
* A Computer Program for Pore Volume and Pore Area Distribution, Rootare & Spencer, 6 Powder Technology, p.&nbsp;17 (1972)<ref name="Rootare1972">{{cite journal|last=Rootare|first=Hillar M.|author2=Judson Spencer|year=1972|title=A computer program for pore volume and pore area distribution calculations from mercury porosimeter data on particulate or porous materials☆|journal=Powder Technology|volume=6|issue=1|pages=17–23|issn=0032-5910|doi=10.1016/0032-5910(72)80051-2|url=https://deepblue.lib.umich.edu/bitstream/2027.42/34072/1/0000351.pdf|hdl=2027.42/34072|hdl-access=free}}</ref>
* Characterization of the Compaction and Sintering of Hydroxyapatite Powders by Mercury Porosimetry,  H.M. Rootare, R.G. Craig, 9 Powder Technology p.&nbsp;199 (1974).
* Thermal Analysis of Experimental and Commercial Gutta-Percha, H.M. Rootare, J.M. Powers, & R.L. Smith, 2 J. Endod. p.&nbsp;244 (Aug. 1976).
* Vapor Phase Adsorption of Water on Hydroxyapatite, H.M. Rootare, R.G. Craig, 56 J. Dent Res. p.&nbsp;1437 (Dec. 1977).
* Preparation of Ag/AgCl Electrodes, H.M. Rootare & J.M. Powers, 11 Journal of Biomedical Materials Research p.&nbsp;633 (1977)
* Free Surface Energy Change for Water Adsorbed on Hydroxyapatite, H.M. Rootare, R.G. Craig, 56 J. Dent Res. p.&nbsp;744 (Jul. 1977).
* Determination of Phase Transitions in Gutta-Percha by Differential Thermal Analysis, H.M. Rootare & J.M. Powers, 56 J. Dent. Res. 1453 (Dec. 1977).
* Sintered Hydroxyapatite Ceramic for Wear studies, H.M. Rootare, J.M. Powers, and R.G. Craig, 57 J. Dent. Res. p.&nbsp;777 (1978).
* Characterization of Hydroxyapatite Powders and Compacts at Room Temperature and After Sintering at 1200 Degrees C., H.M. Rootare, R.G. Craig, 5 J. Or. Reh.  p.&nbsp;293 (1978).
* Wear of Composites by Abrasives of Varying Hardness, H.M. Rootare, J.M. Powers, and R.G. Craig, 58 J. Dent Res. p.&nbsp;1097 (Mar. 1979).
